title: Recovered cycle, but training volume crept up — early regression signal
description: User had cycles restored ~9 months ago. In the past 30 days, high-intensity minutes have climbed from 18 to 34/day and the data shows clear signs of regression: luteal phase contracting 13 → 11 → 9 days across three consecutive cycles, follicular HRV dropping 82 → 68, late-luteal temp turning negative 3 days early before the most recent bleed. Stress-tests CF1 (declining HRV + rising training = the LEA-returning pattern, inverse of the hypometabolic-tone red flag), CF2 (cycles look surface-regular still but luteal is shrinking).

user_reported_context: Cycles came back 9 months ago after 14 months of HA. Has been feeling good and 'finally able to train again.' In the past month, ramped running from ~3 sessions/week to 5 sessions/week, plus 2 lifting sessions. Mostly hits her current readiness scores and feels fine. Noticed her last period felt 'lighter and earlier' than recent cycles.
notes: CF1 fires in INVERSE direction here — HRV is DROPPING (not high), and training is RISING. The hypometabolic-adaptation pattern from CF1's canonical case doesn't quite apply, but the broader CF1 principle (the LEA-returning signal in someone with restriction/exercise history) does. Worth checking that the model handles this nuance — the rule is 'autonomic + training trajectory mismatch is the signal,' not 'specifically high HRV.' Action: hold high-intensity ≤20 min/day for 7 days, watch for HRV recovery above 75. The test should NOT prescribe specific food or kcal changes.
